issues.description: The problem statement refers to the start of the screen memory as screen_buffer, but the template and solution define and use the label display_start. Students instructed to look for or use screen_buffer may not find it in the provided code, causing confusion about which symbol to use or where the screen memory is located.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the name for the screen memory label consistent across artifacts. Either (a) change the problem statement to refer to display_start (the label present in template and solution), or (b) add a matching alias in the template (for example: screen_buffer equ display_start or add a label screen_buffer pointing to the same RESB allocation). This keeps intent clear while preserving the exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the screen buffer as 'screen_buffer' (problem text), but both the template and the solution use the identifier 'display_start' for the same memory base. This naming mismatch can confuse students when they try to map the problem description to the provided code (e.g., where to read/write pixels or which symbol to use in formulas/TODOs).
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single identifier for the screen base across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement to refer to 'display_start' where it currently says 'screen_buffer', or (B) rename the variable 'display_start' in the template and solution to 'screen_buffer'. Update any explanatory comments so all three artifacts use the same name.
